assumptions: A meaningful subset of SMEs receives repeated sustainability requests that free templates do not adequately solve.
Accountants or lenders will distribute the product at acquisition costs compatible with low SME ARPU.
Automated extraction can meet buyer evidence standards with limited human review.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid pilots across multiple independent SMEs documenting request frequency, hours or financing delays avoided, acceptable evidence to lenders or customers, renewal intent, and a signed accountant or lender distribution channel.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: A reusable accounting-linked evidence record can reduce repeated SME work answering lender and large-customer sustainability requests.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Questionnaires can delay finance and onboarding, but request frequency, minimum acceptable evidence, urgency, and SME willingness to pay are unvalidated.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Annual prepaid subscriptions and automated document processing can yield strong margins, though proposed ARPU, low CAC, retention, and 5,000-customer scale depend on channels.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish SMEs receiving finance or supply-chain requests are numerous, but the initial vertical and high-frequency trigger segment are not defined.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Localized evidence extraction provides a wedge, but banks, accountants, accounting suites, and ESG platforms control request and record channels.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: The evidence ledger can expand into tenders, finance applications, energy data, supplier onboarding, risk scoring, and additional EU reporting workflows.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Historical evidence and questionnaire mappings create modest switching costs, but formats are standardized and incumbents can bundle comparable functionality.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Automated evidence-backed reuse can save substantial effort over repeated forms, though free templates may be sufficient for infrequent requests.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The Commission's VSME recommendation and contemplated e-invoice extraction support the workflow, but voluntary status limits urgency.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Accountants and lenders could efficiently aggregate SMEs, but no channel agreement or demonstrated conversion economics exists.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: This is a low-capital, AI-compatible, part-time product, with manageable technical execution but material security, integration, legal-update, and trust requirements.

highest_value_structural_change: Make a lender or accounting platform the embedded distribution and request channel, with the passport accepted directly in finance or supplier workflows.
main_structural_strength: The concept is technically and financially lightweight to test and can create a reusable data asset around recurring external evidence requests.
primary_score_limiter: The voluntary standard, free alternatives, and unproven request frequency create weak urgency and uncertain ARPU without controlled channel distribution.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: VSME is explicitly voluntary and burden-reducing, so free templates or bundled accounting and bank tools may satisfy most small firms at little incremental cost.
